images.caption: This is a map of the footprint of the 2015 Northern California's Lake, Colusa, and Yolo counties, where the fire burned more than 69,000 acres and burned 96 structures. This image was made in QGIS using data from the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire), the National Hydrography Dataset (NHD), OpenStreetMap, USGS, and others.

images.caption:
The Rocky Fire in Lake County, California, is generating enough smoke to be seen from space. The fire is located in Lower Lake, about 30 miles north of Santa Rosa.
The Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) instrument that flies aboard NASA's Terra satellite captured an image of smoke from the Rocky Fire near Clearlake, California, on July 30, 2015, at 18:45 UTC (2:45 p.m. EDT). The multiple red pixels are heat signatures (red) detected by MODIS. The smoke appears to be a light brown color.

images.caption: Capt. Josiah Faber, company commander of Task Force Charlie, Guam Army National Guard, in the Jerusalem Fire in Lake County, California, watches a Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE) aircraft drop fire retardant Aug. 12 on a hilltop east of Clearlake, California. Faber, also commander of Alpha Company, 1st Battalion, 18th Cavalry Regiment, 578th Brigade Engineer Battalion, leads more than 120 Soldiers involved in the Rocky Fire, adjacent to the Jerusalem Fire. (U.S. Army National Guard photo/Staff Sgt. Eddie Siguenza)
images.alt: Capt. Faber, also commander of Alpha Company, 1st Battalion, 18th Cavalry Regiment, 578th Brigade Engineer Battalion, leads more than 120 Soldiers involved in the Rocky Fire, adjacent to the Jerusalem Fire. images.caption: A launch and retrieve team from the 132nd Multirole Bridge Company (MRBC), California Army National Guard, uses a steel guide line to move a ramp and bay over Cache Creek River Aug. 7 at Cache Creek National Park in Yolo County, California. The platforms are part of a floating bridge the MRBC constructed to help CAL FIRE vehicles and equipment cross the river to battle the Rocky Fire. (U.S. Army National Guard photo/Staff Sgt. Eddie Siguenza)

images.caption: Spc. Justin Castillo, an aircraft engineer with the California National Guard's B Company, 1-126th Aviation Regiment, observes a water pick-up during the Rocky Fire near Clearlake, Calif., Aug. 1. During his crew’s 2.5 hour firefighting mission, they conducted 18 water drops. (U.S. Army National Guard photo/ Sgt. Jason Beal/ released)
